title: Attack: which monster, from where, and how
tagline: Pure fight decisions: whom to hit, where to stand, which move, which attack.
summary: The attack layer turns positions on the map into fighting decisions, without pressing keys or reading the clock. It ports the game client's own targeting rules (reach), decides the next move up close or at range (stance), picks the monster to hit (target) and the attack to use (choice), and measures how dangerous a place is (danger) to choose where to stand (spots, ropes) and what a knock-back costs (knock). The behavior layer calls it every look; control turns its answers into keys.
details_md:
**Where it sits.** Each look, perception and localization produce a `Scene` (her place, the monsters placed on platforms). `behavior` (the fight loop, the hunt loop, grinding) asks this layer what to do and hands the answer to `control.actions`. The layer may import only perception, localization and motion (`tests/test_architecture.py`), and nothing in it reads the clock, starts a thread or touches a file: the functions are computations over map units, so the simulator and the tests run exactly the same decisions as the live game. The only state is in-memory caches (per map or platform) and `magic`'s process-wide swap of module constants; the only outside reads are two environment switches in `stance` (`GAMELAB_JUMP_ASIDE`, `GAMELAB_HOP_UP`).

**The foundation is reach** (`reach.py`): the game client's targeting ported from RustMS's v83 client and checked against live logs. A ground attack first swipes with the claw if a monster is in its 65-unit box, else the star's banded search (bands 20 wide from 65 to 400 ahead, windows widening 1 unit up and down per 4 ahead) picks the first body it overlaps, and one line from 28 units over her feet to that pick must not cross her own floor going down or a wall of her foothold group. From a jump the same search runs from wherever her feet are at the attack's start. `reach.shots` lists every jump and attack key that surely hits each monster.

**The move** (`stance.py`): `stance()` for a group and `decide()` for one target return a small *act* tuple (throw, jump-throw, jump back, step away, close in, wait). Since 2026-10-27 every decision is made for the moment her attack will actually start (`Pace`): her remaining attack lock, the look's age and each monster's walk from its track. Up close she escapes by least danger, throws only where the attack surely takes the monster, or steps to where the next one will; at range she picks the side to throw, a passing jump, or a jump shot when nothing on the ground reaches.

**The monster and the attack** (`target.py`, `choice.py`): the target-first planner (2026-11-04) scores every monster as (chance it's there) x EXP / (time to an attack + time to kill), keeps its pick unless another scores 1.3x as much, switches for one coming at her, and plans the next. With it on, behavior hands the stance that one monster as `wanted` and the rest as `among`, so the stance decides the move against the chosen target only. The attack choice uses Lucky Seven unless MP is short, nothing is seen in the throw's way, or the regular attack would finish the monster about as fast, reckoning a monster's HP left as a probability distribution.

**Danger and places** (`danger.py`, `spots.py`, `ropes.py`, `knock.py`): danger is the expected share of her HP touches take soon at a place, from each kind's touch damage (game formula) and how soon it can walk to her, summed over seen monsters and unexplained spawn points. It sets how near a hard-hitting monster may come (`keep_off`: a Horny Mushroom 169 units), scores shooting spots (coverage minus danger), picks rope heights, and guards against respawns. `knock` flies a touch's knock-back like the simulator and prices it in EXP; it is built but not yet wired into decisions.

**Characters.** The thief's values are the module constants. For the magician, `magic.apply` overwrites reach's search constants and several stance switches at the start of a hunting command (her Magic Claw: 50 to 300 ahead, nothing stops it, never cast mid-jump), the quick way the user asked for on 2026-10-28.

**How it's tuned.** Almost every rule is a module constant or boolean switch with its evidence in a comment: live telemetry hours on Tree Dungeon, frame-by-frame clip reviews, and paired simulator runs. Switches let a rule be turned off to reproduce the earlier behaviour for A/B runs and golden traces.

modules.title: Reach
modules.tagline: The game client's targeting, ported: claw swipe, star search, line of sight, jump shots.
modules.summary: Answers 'would an attack from here hit that monster?' the way the game client decides it: the claw swipes anything in its box up close, else the star's banded target search picks the first body it overlaps, and one line from her to that pick is checked against walls and floors. It also lists every jump and attack key that surely hits each monster from where she stands (`shots`, `Coverage`). Everything else in the layer measures reach through this module.
modules.details_md:
**Measured facts it starts from** (Thicket Around the Beach II): a star flies 400 map units, hits monsters 60 units below or above her, leaves her about 530 ms after the key and flies about 690 units/s. What it hits is decided when the attack **starts** (about 65 ms after the key), from the monsters' bodies in the game data; the flying star is only a picture.

**From the ground, two stages** (a port of the v83 client's decompiled shot code as RustMS has it, cross-checked against meowdb's pages):

1. **The claw first.** Each attack takes one of two stab stances at random (`CLAW_STANCES`: stabO1, stabO2). Its box from the game data is cut to `CLAW_FAR` (65) ahead. The nearest monster whose body reaches into it is swiped (9-11 damage, no star), on her level or not: the client has no level gate. `claw_edge(half)` = 65 + half its width + `CLAW_MARGIN` (12) is how far off a monster must be for a throw to be a star: a pig 111, an Orange Mushroom 109, a slime or a Green/Horny Mushroom 105, a snail 96.
2. **The star's search.** Bands `SEARCH_STEP` (20) wide from `SEARCH_START` (65) to `STAR_RANGE` (400): 17 bands. Band k's window runs from 12 - 5k to 44 + 5k units above her feet (centred on `SHOT_H` = 28, the client's own constant). The star goes to a body overlapping the **first** band any body overlaps. Within that band the client takes the monster that entered the map first, which can't be seen, so `take_chances` splits it evenly.

`ground_sure(half)` packages this as the nearest and farthest a ground attack surely takes a level monster: (claw_edge, `SHOT_RANGE` 410). `shot_dx` gives the nearest sideways for one off her level (60 below, an Orange Mushroom from 113, a pig 151, a snail 246). `can_shoot` is band and distance only; `can_hit` adds terrain and shielding and is the call almost everyone makes.

**What stops a star** (`LINE` = 'v83', the default since 2026-10-21): one line, from `SHOT_H` above her feet to where the star hits the picked monster's body (`hit_point`). A floor of any foothold group stops it going **down** through, so her own platform blocks a star at a monster below unless she stands near enough its end. Walls stop it only if they belong to her own foothold group and only going in at their outer face (`faces`). `sight_stop` is the port of RustMS's `blocked`, including the corner rule; since 2026-11-01 footholds are found through a 64-unit grid (`_Sight`, `SIGHT_CELL`). Because the client checks only its pick's line, a monster picked first whose line is stopped **shields** everything behind it (`shielded`). `clear_length` is a numpy-vectorised version that `spots` uses over tens of thousands of lines.

**From a jump** (`AIR_MODEL` = 'search' since 2026-10-27): the same search from wherever her feet are when the attack starts, with no claw. `air_sure` requires the pick to hold `AIR_MARGIN` (6) deep at both ends of the decide lag. Keyed 40 ms after the jump key (her feet 21-26 up) a Green or Horny Mushroom on her level is surely picked from 44 ahead; keyed 120 ms (an air turn, feet 52-56 up), only from 144.

**Every shot from here** (`shots` -> `Coverage`): for each wanted monster a ground Shot if `can_hit`, and for each jump kind (`up`, `forward`, `back`) and side, two attack keys a jump (the user's, 2026-11-01): the soonest (`KEY_FIRST_MS` 40, or a turn's 120) and the top's (`TOP_KEY_MS` 278). A key is sure only if keying it 15 ms sooner or later (checked every 5 ms) picks the same monster with a clear line; the jitter room (`JITTER_FIRST_MS` 15 later, `JITTER_TOP_MS` 20 either way) is narrowed to where that holds. Landings and their variants come from `motion.physics`. `key_pick` says what an attack starting now would take ('claw', 'star', 'stopped', 'nothing'): the hunter logs it at every key and stance's jump-aside asks it.

Several module constants are switches kept for probes and A/B runs (`WALLS_BLOCK`, `LINE`, `UP_BY_SEARCH`, `RAMP_BELOW`, `AIR_SEARCH`, `CLIENT_HIT_POINT`), and `attack.magic` overwrites the search constants for the magician at a command's start.

key_items.name: can_hit
key_items.signature: def can_hit(platform, x, y, m, reach=SHOT_RANGE, rise=0.0, target=None, others=(), sizes=None) -> bool
key_items.summary: Whether a star from (x, y) hits monster m: in reach by its body (can_shoot), its line not stopped (wall_to), and no monster the attack takes first has its line stopped (shielded).
key_items.details_md: The single most-called reach question: stance, target, spots and behavior all go through it. It doesn't ask whether m is the pick *now*: a clear monster in front only orders the kills.

key_items.name: search_band
key_items.signature: def search_band(near, far, bottom, top, top0=None, floor0=None) -> int | None
key_items.summary: The first band of the star's search a body overlaps (strictly, as the client's IntersectRect), or None.
key_items.details_md: Bands start at SEARCH_START and are SEARCH_STEP wide; window(k) (line 339) gives each band's vertical extent: SHOT_H -/+ spread(k), spread(k) = (65 + 20k) // 4, i.e. 12 - 5k to 44 + 5k above her feet, one unit up and one down for every four ahead, as the client's.

key_items.name: can_shoot
key_items.signature: def can_shoot(dx, dy, reach=SHOT_RANGE, kind=None, sizes=None) -> bool
key_items.summary: Band and distance alone, terrain aside: the target is within 60 above/below her (or higher where the search's windows reach, with UP_BY_SEARCH) and between shot_dx and min(reach, max_dx) sideways.
key_items.details_md: can_hit is this plus the line-of-sight and shield checks; decide() and _clear_from use it directly for walk goals. Its default `reach` is bound at import, which is why magic.apply rewrites can_shoot.__defaults__.

key_items.name: attack_chances
key_items.signature: def attack_chances(bodies, claw=None, band=None) -> list[tuple[float, float]]
key_items.summary: Each monster's chance of being swiped by the claw and of taking the star, for one ground attack.
key_items.details_md: Per claw stance (each half the time) the nearest body in its box is swiped; otherwise the star's share is split evenly among the monsters in the first band. take_chances sums the two.

key_items.name: claw_edge
key_items.signature: def claw_edge(half: float) -> float
key_items.summary: How far off a level monster must be for a ground throw not to be a claw swipe: CLAW_FAR + half + CLAW_MARGIN.
key_items.details_md: A pig 111, Orange Mushroom 109, slime 105, snail 96.

key_items.name: ground_sure
key_items.signature: def ground_sure(half: float) -> tuple[float, float]
key_items.summary: The nearest and farthest a ground attack surely takes a level monster: (claw_edge(half), SHOT_RANGE).
key_items.details_md: The seam the stance's ground decisions go through (too_close, close_to, _from_here, _clear_step, landing).

key_items.name: shot_dx
key_items.signature: def shot_dx(dy, kind=None, sizes=None) -> float
key_items.summary: The nearest sideways a ground throw at a monster dy below (+) or above (-) her throws a star that picks it.
key_items.details_md: Max of the search's min_dx by its body, the claw's reach (claw_dx), and the old ramp below her (ramp_dx, while RAMP_BELOW).

key_items.name: wall_between
key_items.signature: def wall_between(platform, x, y, tx, rise=0.0, target=None, shot_h=None, ty=None, body=None, line=None, client=None, row_start=None) -> Segment | None
key_items.summary: What stops a star from her to a monster at tx by the chosen line: a wall of her foothold group, or (v83) a floor it goes down through.
key_items.details_md: With CLIENT_HIT_POINT the client's own hit point is checked too where it falls outside the target's platform. wall_in_way wraps it (None with WALLS_BLOCK off); wall_to takes a Monster.

key_items.name: sight_stop
key_items.signature: def sight_stop(platform, sx, sy, ex, ey, footholds=None) -> Segment | None
key_items.summary: Port of the v83 client's line-of-sight test (RustMS ShotPath.h blocked): the first foothold the line crosses from its open to its closed side.
key_items.details_md: Footholds come from the platform's cached grid (_Sight, SIGHT_CELL 64).

key_items.name: shielded
key_items.signature: def shielded(platform, x, y, m, others, rise=0.0) -> Monster | None
key_items.summary: A monster the attack picks before m whose own line is stopped: then no star reaches m from here.
key_items.details_md: From the ground, one in an earlier search band; from a jump, a nearer one in the attack's area. A monster in the claw's box is never a shield (a swipe has no line).

key_items.name: air_sure
key_items.signature: def air_sure(ahead, dy, top, half, gap_ms, margin=AIR_MARGIN) -> bool
key_items.summary: Whether an attack keyed gap_ms after the jump key of a jump in place surely picks a monster: air_takes, margin deep, at both ends of the decide lag.
key_items.details_md: Keyed 40 ms: a mushroom on her level from 44 ahead; keyed 120 ms: from 144.

key_items.name: shots
key_items.signature: def shots(model, platform, x, y, monsters, sizes=None, kinds=JUMP_KINDS, where=None, others=None, lands=None) -> list[Shot]
key_items.summary: Every attack from (x, y) that surely hits one of `monsters`: from the ground and from each kind of jump, at the sooner of its two attack keys that is sure.
key_items.details_md: Poses come from physics.pose; picks from _air_pick at both ends of the decide lag with a clear wall_in_way line; a key counts only if keys KEY_SLACK_MS either side pick the same monster. `where` walks the monsters to their predicted x; `lands` skips jumps that don't land her back in a stretch (the stance's only).

key_items.name: Coverage
key_items.signature: class Coverage(shot_list: list[Shot])
key_items.summary: shots indexed by monster: of(m), hits(m, kinds), ground(m), best(m) (ground first, else the soonest key).
key_items.details_md: Built lazily by behavior.fight's jump_cover and passed to stance as the `jumps` callback.

key_items.name: Shot
key_items.signature: @dataclass(frozen=True) class Shot
key_items.summary: One way to hit a target: side, the jump (None: from the ground), its attack key and jitter window, where she is at the pick, and where the jump lands (with its variants).
key_items.details_md: lands_sure / land_span / lands_back check every variant of the jump (early or late lift-off, slower, the kick short).

decisions.what: The v83 client's line (LINE 'v83') became the default: her own floor stops a star at a monster below unless she stands near its end.
decisions.why: The user, watching her hunt, saw her own platform stop her stars at monsters below, down a step and from a higher platform onto a lower one.

decisions.what: UP_BY_SEARCH on: ground throws reach monsters more than 60 above her where the search's windows do.
decisions.why: The user's choice ('Turn it on now'): their own play killed Green Mushrooms 69-100 above from the ground; in the simulator +21.8% EXP. The review had called the evidence suggestive, not decisive.

decisions.what: AIR_SEARCH: from a jump the search's widening windows pick too, not only a fixed area around her feet.
decisions.why: The user's play: of 30 kills of monsters 15+ above her, 23 fit the search; the user: 'remember the widening vertical search as horizontal scale out'.

decisions.what: TURN_KEY_MS raised to 120 ms (85 until then).
decisions.why: Keyed 85 ms after the jump key, 36% of the turns in the air went the wrong way live.

decisions.what: AIR_MODEL 'search': from a jump the star's search alone picks, from her feet when the attack starts.
decisions.why: 788 live jump throws on Tree Dungeon fit it 111 log-likelihood better than the area model; matches RustMS having no case for the air.

decisions.what: Two attack keys a jump (at once and at the top) with a little jitter, instead of scanning every key from the soonest to 480 ms.
decisions.why: The user: 'You only need two jump attacks: one with jump and immediately attack, another with jump and attack at mid air peak', and 'add a bit jitter ... can later on analyze if the jitter can show any pattern'. The scan was ~89 keys a start, most of the search's time.

decisions.what: Line-of-sight footholds found through a 64-unit grid (_Sight).
decisions.why: The latency analysis: trying every floor and wall was 40% of the slowest jump-shot searches' time (59 us a line, 4 with the grid).

decisions.what: CLIENT_HIT_POINT: check the line to the client's own hit point too.
decisions.why: Cornered study R6: of her jumps in place up close, the 21 whose line to that point is stopped did damage 2 times, the 184 clear 80 times (p 0.0015).

gotchas: SEARCH_TOP0 (44) is the client's value but the shot logs lean to 21; the comment calls it 'the one number to change (to 21)' if the top-60 probe finds the lower top. Too high has her throw at monsters above her the star doesn't take.

Within the first band the client takes whichever monster entered the map first, which can't be seen: take_chances splits the star evenly, so a 'sure' pick only exists when a monster is alone in its band.
The claw has no level gate: a monster above or below her whose body reaches into the stab box is swiped instead of shot.

magic.apply overwrites this module's constants at runtime and patches can_hit/can_shoot's default `reach` via __defaults__ (bound at import). Code that copied a constant by name at import keeps the thief's value unless magic swaps that copy too (it does for spots.SHOT_RANGE).
_sight caches its grid on the Platform object itself (`platform._sight`), rebuilt if the platform's floors or walls tuple changes.
Between her level and 60 below her the search is unchecked in game and the only logged throws go against it, hence RAMP_BELOW keeping the older ramp.

Modules that import reach's constants by name keep the thief's values when magic swaps reach: gamelab/ui/render.py and ui/web.py import SHOT_UP, SHOT_DOWN and STAR_REACH so, and only spots.SHOT_RANGE is swapped among such copies.

modules.title: Stance
modules.tagline: From positions to one act: throw, jump-throw, jump back, step away, close in, wait.
modules.summary: The fight's move policy. `stance()` decides for a group of monsters (fight.clear, tours, the hunt loop) and `decide()` for one target (fight.kill, `hunt kill`); `pick_target` orders who goes first. Every decision is judged at the moment her next attack will actually start (`Pace`), so a monster walking at her is treated as where it will be, not where it was seen. It also prices landings and says how much of a platform she may use.
modules.details_md:
**Inputs.** `wanted`: whom she means to hit; `around`: every monster about her (they shield, block moves, add danger). With the target-first planner on, `wanted` is its one chosen monster and `among` the others nearby, which shape her room but get no answer.

**The answer is a tuple** (an *act*): `('throw', side)`, `('jump_throw', side[, JumpPlan])`, `('jump_back', side[, JumpPlan])`, `('back', side, units[, AWAY])` (step away), `('approach', side, units)`, or `('wait',)`. `decide()` answers `('throw', side)`, `('walk', side, units)` or `('skip', reason)`. `behavior.fight` logs it (`act_text`); `control.actions` keys it.

**Timing first** (`Pace`, from 2026-10-27): a decision asks where each monster will be when the attack starts: `lead` (her attack lock left plus the look's age) + `GROUND_PICK_S` (~0.07 s: key lag plus half the decide lag) + `TAP_S` (0.08 s) if she must turn. A monster walks by its track's speed; one walking at her stops where their bodies meet (`PACE_STOP`); one she just hit stands until `FLINCH_HOLD_S`. `too_close` then asks whether a ground throw at that predicted spot would be a claw swipe (`reach.ground_sure`) or nearer than its danger allows (`Danger.keep_off`).

**`stance()` in order:**
1. Sort the monsters: `mine` (on her platform, or on one just under or over whose body meets hers: `beside`, `BESIDE`), `close` (mine and too close), `reachable` (`reach.can_hit` by the game's body sizes).
2. **Up close** (`_close_quarters_here`): the nearest close monster on the side she faces decides (with `FIRST_TO_REACH`, the other side's nearest if both throws are sure and it reaches her first, or a sure throw that way instead of an unsure jump in place). A kind that hits hard, or a touch she must clear before her invulnerability ends (`FIGHT_CLEAR`), goes to `_escape`: of a jump back, steps away and a throw from here, the least danger (`Danger.at`), a step only if `ESCAPE_THROW` (0.03) safer, and with `ESCAPE_UP` a jump up onto a platform overhead. Otherwise: a sure throw from here (`_from_here`: from the ground past the claw's edge, else a jump in place keyed 40 ms, an air turn at 120 ms, or a tap first); else the shortest step after which her next throw surely takes it (`_clear_step`, 15 to 120 units every 10); else a jump back (`JUMP_BACK_ROOM` 110 behind, nobody within `JUMP_BACK_CLEAR` 160); else, under a platform overhead, a plain step away; else the throw anyway (the claw within `CLAW_ONLY` 15, else a jump in place). Never into a monster's body (`_into`) nor onto a free spawn point (`_on_spawn`), and at most `MAX_MOVES` (2) moves in a row without a throw.
3. **Something in reach:** in passing, a jump forward that hits on the way (`PASSING_JUMPS`); else `_throw_side` picks the way: an imminent toucher, then her wounds (`WOUNDS_FIRST`), then a toucher on her platform (`TOUCHER_FIRST`), then the way she faces, then the side with more. A touch from a monster the looks miss (`clawed`) makes it a jump throw instead where one surely picks the target, since the air has no claw (`CLAWED_AIR`).
4. **Nothing in reach:** a jump shot from `reach.Coverage` (`_jump_shot`: landing back on her platform however the jump goes, her body clear of every monster along the arc every 0.02 s, landing danger at most `JUMP_DANGER` worse, landing with clearance); else step out from under a monster off her level; else close in to `SHOT_RANGE - 40`; else wait.

**Room on the platform:** `_stand_limits` keeps `EDGE_MARGIN` (25) from the ends, plus `KNOCKBACK_ROOM` (25) with monsters about. Steps away keep `DROP_ROOM` (100) from an end with a long drop (`drop_limits`: next platform `LONG_DROP` 100 or more below, `end_drop`); up close, `move_limits` lets her go to `WALL_ROOM` (her half width + 3) of a wall end (both cached per platform).

**Landings** (`landing`, `landing_of`, `Prices`): a landing whose first attack isn't sure to take the nearest monster costs `LANDING_PRICE_S` (1.36 s of hunting); one where a monster walks into her `MEET_PRICE_S` (2.86 s) more; with `Prices` the caller's map-specific numbers. The navigator's landing chains use it too.

Most rules are boolean module constants, their evidence in comments, so each can be switched off for an A/B run; `attack.magic` switches several off for the magician (`POINT_BLANK`, `FIGHT_CLEAR`, `ESCAPE_UP`, `PASSING_JUMPS`). The jump aside and the hop up (`_aside`, `_hop`) exist but are off unless `GAMELAB_JUMP_ASIDE=1` / `GAMELAB_HOP_UP=1`.

decisions.what: JUMP_THROW_SNAILS False: a snail too close for a ground star is never jump-thrown at; she steps back or stabs it.
decisions.why: The user saw jump throws mostly miss snails, 'especially on short platform[s]'; the day's telemetry: 5 of 26 jump throws at a snail under 46 units off hurt it.

decisions.what: A passing jump must land no more than PASS_SLACK past where she is going.
decisions.why: Review: overshooting a rope's foot or a takeoff by 15-80 units had her walk back, which a ground throw doesn't.

decisions.what: DROP_ROOM / LONG_DROP, ESCAPE_UP and TOUCHER_FIRST added.
decisions.why: Live on 2026-10-25 three knocks took her off Tree Dungeon 23's left end, 389 units down and 43 s back up; 24's Green made 14 of her 34 touches.

decisions.what: Clearance kept ahead of time: decisions go by where each monster will be when the attack starts (Pace), with CLEAR_MARGIN and CLAW_ONLY.
decisions.why: The user: 'I frequently find the player standing at the same X pos as the mob, doing jump hit but couldn't hit the mob because no minimal clearance is maintained'. Live, a monster within 60 on her platform 8.7 s a minute, 27% of her attacks.

decisions.what: Landings priced by what her first attack there would take; up close she moves away to where her next attack surely takes the monster.
decisions.why: The user: 'the character should actively try to move away from the mob to attack it.' A not-sure landing cost 5.7 EXP and 0.13 touches live.

decisions.what: PACE_STOP: a monster walking at her stops where their bodies meet.
decisions.why: Walking through her, a walker within ~85 in front had her tap round and throw at her empty back (86 such throws in the goldens).

decisions.what: FIGHT_CLEAR (evade work R8): touched, she gets clear of the monster on her before her invulnerability ends.
decisions.why: Live 53 of 148 touches came within 2 s of the one before; a fight stayed on a Horny Mushroom for three windows in the simulator.

decisions.what: WOUNDS_FIRST: throw the way of her most-hurt target and wait for a hidden one, unless a monster is imminent.
decisions.why: 166 of 1,497 first casts left a monster alive with no second cast for 8 s; the user: 'yes we should finish a monster, but we should also watch out for inmennent danger from a close by mob'.

decisions.what: POINT_BLANK off for the magician (via attack.magic).
decisions.why: Her close quarters' jump throws went out as ground casts: 106 of 540 casts, 62% showing nothing.

decisions.what: BESIDE on: monsters on a platform just under or over hers count as on hers where their bodies meet.
decisions.why: The user's choice of 'more exp and loot': +19.7 EXP a minute and 4.3 fewer hurting touches over 12 seeds.

decisions.what: TOUCH_EXP set from the user's prices (28), and Prices lets callers price landings with the map's own numbers.
decisions.why: Review: one map's monster and rate had been frozen into general constants.

decisions.what: ROOM_LINE: a jump throw's later jitter keys have their line checked too.
decisions.why: On a slope later keys' stars were stopped where the first key's hit (185 of 4,150 keys in the world's close throws).

decisions.what: CLAWED_AIR and CLAWED_CLOSE (cornered study R1): after a touch by a monster the looks missed, throw from a jump in place where it is sure.
decisions.why: From the ground the press goes to the claw; in that hour 59 of 586 ground Lucky Sevens aimed 105+ off with nothing seen within 105 took no MP, and every one checked on the frames was the claw on a monster the looks missed.

decisions.what: FIRST_TO_REACH (cornered study R8): up close, throw at whichever monster reaches her first, and prefer a sure throw the other way over an unsure jump in place.
decisions.why: BugBaby's hour: 6 jumps in place at a monster they didn't surely take, with a sure one on her other side, none doing damage.

decisions.what: Jump aside and hop up added, both off by default (GAMELAB_JUMP_ASIDE, GAMELAB_HOP_UP).
decisions.why: The user on the no-hit clips: 'no, jump aside and attack from a distance'; the pre-registered whole-run test failed on attacks at nothing, so both stay off.

gotchas: Thresholds built on reach's constants are read at call time, so magic.apply's swaps reach them; the one cache (_JUMP_REACH) is cleared by magic.
decide() and stance() use different closeness rules: decide uses TOO_CLOSE (110) or close_to by positions as seen; stance uses too_close by where monsters will be (Pace) plus danger.
MAX_MOVES only counts where something on the map is a danger (danger.any); on the first map stance behaves as before.
Only ('back', side, units, AWAY) counts toward MAX_MOVES; _step_from_under's and held_step's steps have no AWAY.
By danger alone a step away always beat a jump back or a throw (it goes 120 to the jump's 95), so ESCAPE_THROW (a guess) biases toward throwing.
stance's knock model (end_drop looking 5 units past an end, margins of 25, 50, 100) disagrees with attack.knock's flown model; the README says replacing it is the planner's work.
Per-platform caches (_MOVES, _DROPS) are keyed by id(model) and keep the model itself so its id can't be reused while cached; cleared past 4096 entries.
SMALL_STEP_END is only used when SNAIL_FAR_END is on, which it isn't.

modules.title: Target
modules.tagline: Target-first planner: score monsters by EXP per second, keep the pick, plan the next.
modules.summary: Picks the one monster she hits next (the primary) and the one after it (the next), from a closed-form score per monster recomputed at every look: EXP over the seconds to get an attack on it and kill it. It keeps the primary unless another beats it by 30%, switches for a monster coming at her, and on the whole-screen setting also weighs places where she can hit a pile. Pure: what perception says comes in as `Her` and `Foe`s, no clock, no keys, no simulation.

decisions.what: The target-first planner: one monster to hit, a closed-form score per monster, no rollouts; on by default (GAMELAB_TARGET=0 turns it off).
decisions.why: The user: 'planner should just decide which mob to hit and plan against that. This is simple, less costly, and easy to follow.'

decisions.why: The user: 'watch for respawns at each frame ... change target if a mob is moving towards you and can knock you back, if you are not already attacking that mob ... think about what's your next target'.

decisions.what: The whole screen: every monster on screen is a candidate, places on other platforms via the navigator, piles weighed (GAMELAB_SCREEN=0 off).
decisions.why: The user: 'You aren't really looking at all mobs on the screen ... factor in piled up mobs and lean towards going to a place where you can hit a bunch of piled up mobs.'

modules.title: Danger
modules.tagline: How much of her HP monster touches would soon take at a place.
modules.summary: Puts one number on a place (a platform and an x, or a height on a rope): the expected share of her HP monster touches would take in the next moments. Each kind's touch is computed from the game data with the game's damage formula; whether and how soon it can reach her comes from its platform, speed and body. Spots, the stance's keep-off and escapes, the hunt loop's waiting place and rope refuges all compare places by it, never by a kind or map name.
modules.details_md:
**What a touch takes** (`touch_taken`, the formula from meowdb's damage-taken page and the osms datamine, which agree): raw = PADamage x (1.2 + 0.2u); taken = raw x (1 - DEF / (DEF + 300 + 2 raw)) - (DEF/25 + level/10), truncated, at least 1. `u` is the roll (0.5 by default). Her DEF is perception's (her stat window, else fitted to her touches); `DEFENCE` (75) is only the prior. A kind whose touch is under `DANGER_MIN` (5% of her HP) counts for nothing: at level 19 a pig takes 1.7% of her 642 HP, so on the first map nothing counts (`Danger.any` is False) and every decision there behaves as before the model. On Tree Dungeon a Horny Mushroom takes about 16% of her 752 HP at level 24, a Green Mushroom 7.2%.

**Whether it can reach her** (`Danger.walk`): a monster walks only its own platform, turning where the game turns it (`walk_edges`). One on a platform just under or over hers touches her where their bodies overlap (`level`: its floor less than its top under her feet, or less than her height `HER_TALL` over them). A kind that hops (`MapModel.mob_hops`) can reach a platform within `HOP_ACROSS`/`HOP_UP` (60/60), weighted `HOP_CHANCE` (0.25, a guess). Fliers go straight at her.

**How soon:** the walk to where its body meets hers at its speed, weighted `soon(t) = exp(-t / THREAT_S)` with `THREAT_S` = 1.7 s (about two of her throws). A Horny Mushroom at 100 units/s counts 0.71 at 100 units off, 0.39 at 200, 0.12 at 400.

**The danger at a place** (`Danger.at`) is the sum over sources of share x chance x soon. Sources (`_sources`) are the monsters a look saw plus the spawn points they don't account for (per platform and kind, the unexplained fraction of points, each as one that may respawn now); with no look, every spawn point's monster at its point (the planning picture `spots` uses).

**What it decides elsewhere:**
- `keep_off(kind)`: how near a monster on her platform may come before she moves: where its danger reaches `KEEP_DANGER` (8% of her HP): half + `HER_HALF` + speed x `THREAT_S` x ln(share / 0.08). A Horny Mushroom 169 units; a Green Mushroom (7.2%) 0, i.e. only the claw's reach.
- `of(kind, q, mx, p, x)`: one monster's share x chance x soon at a place: what `at` sums, and what stance's `too_close` asks for one beside her on another platform.
- `beside`: whether a monster on a neighbouring platform counts as on hers (stance's BESIDE).
- `free_points`: spawn points no seen monster accounts for (the stance never steps onto one).
- `respawn_points` / `respawn_risk`: the spawn guard (from 2026-11-03): free points within `RESPAWN_NEAR` (70) of where she would stand, no monster within `SPAWN_CLEAR` (100), risk = fill x (`NEWBORN_TOUCH` 0.85 - `NEWBORN_SEEN` 0.29) x share x the chance her stay overlaps the map's spawn pass (`PASS_BEFORE` 0.15 s, `PASS_AFTER` 1.0 s).
- `on_rope` / `walk_rope`: the same for hanging on a rope at a height (a monster touches her only if its body, up to its highest frame, `mob_tall`, reaches hers).
- `taken(kind)`: the share a touch takes even under DANGER_MIN (for prices); an unknown kind is charged the map's hardest-touching kind.

`of_map` builds one `Danger` per (map, her, least) and keeps up to 8; `every_kind` is the same with every touching kind counted (`least` 0), for `behavior.retreat`, since a place to stay a while should count even weak touches.

modules.title: Spots
modules.tagline: Where to stand to shoot a platform: most of it in reach, least danger, nearest.
modules.summary: For a platform she wants to hunt (a 'ground'), finds places on other platforms from which most of it is in a star's reach, scores them by that coverage less the danger there, and picks the nearest of the nearly-best ones she can safely stand on. If none qualifies she hunts the ground standing on it, from its safest place. Used by the hunt loop and tours.
modules.details_md:
**Coverage** (`coverage`): the fraction of the target platform's length a star from (x, y) reaches either way, at a monster of a kind (a pig by default): within `shot_dx`..`SHOT_RANGE` sideways, inside the band (60 up/down), clipped by her foothold group's walls (`reach.clear_span`) and, by the v83 line, only where no floor stops it (`reach.clear_length`, vectorised). So to shoot down, a place near her platform's end covers most: 17 is shot from 14 at x 756.

**The grid** (`_grid`): every `X_STEP` (10) units along every platform, `EDGE_MARGIN` (25) in from its ends, with coverage > 0, paired with the danger there as planned (`Danger.at` with no look: every spawn point's monster at its point). A spot's **score** is coverage - `DANGER_WEIGHT` (1.0) x danger. `_spots` takes each platform's best x and sorts safe platforms first (`MapModel.safe`: no monster can touch her there), then by score.

**Off spawn points** (`_off_spawns`, from 2026-10-26): on a platform where kinds that count spawn, a spot keeps `SPAWN_CLEAR` (50: a monster's half width and hers) from those points, giving way on knock room at an end with a short drop if it must, as long as the best such place scores within the touch share of the kind whose point the best spot sits on. Spots on such platforms also keep `GROUND_MARGIN` (50) from the ends.

**Choosing** (`spot`): candidates are spots on other platforms with at least `MIN_COVERAGE` (0.3) of the ground in reach that she may stand on: `spot_ok` (nobody worth hunting can touch her there) or, with danger, scoring better than hunting the ground itself (`_ground_score` = 1 - danger at its safest place). Of those scoring at least best - 30% (`NEAR_BEST` 0.7), the nearest by travel time (`travel`, the route planner's; `UNREACHABLE` without a route). Else `on_ground`: the ground's safest place (its middle where nothing counts). `spot_for` looks for a spot reaching more of the monsters still left, so she keeps shooting from safety instead of dropping into the pile; `spot_at` / `best_spot` give the plan-time spot for a sweep.

On Tree Dungeon, 23 (two Horny Mushrooms) is shot from 24 at x 221 (97.9% of 23 in reach), where only 24's Green Mushroom can touch her.

Everything is cached per map in `_KEPT` (up to 4 maps) keyed also by her (`_her`) and by reach's switches (`_switches`: WALLS_BLOCK, LINE, the search window, CLAW, RAMP_BELOW), because a platform's spots take 3.6 ms and all of Tree Dungeon's grounds with danger 1.1 s.

modules.title: Knock
modules.tagline: Where a touch's knock-back leaves her, flown like the simulator, and what it costs.
modules.summary: Simulates a touch's knock-back exactly as the simulator's world does (270 units/s away and up, no steering, the game's walls, a slide to a stop or off an end) and tables the answers per platform for microsecond lookups. `cost` prices a knock off her platform in EXP: the time lost getting back plus the touches expected on the way. Built as the planner's knock term; not wired into decisions yet.
modules.details_md:
**Why.** The arrival study of 2026-11-03 found that no decision priced where a touch's knock throws her and that the stack's knock models were wrong. The user: "Motion planning should consider the current game situation and dynamically calculate the best action to perform". This module is that knock term (prerequisite A); nothing decides by it yet.

**The flight** (`fly`, `_launched`): from her feet at x on a platform, on the ground (`GROUND`) or mid-jump at a height (only the height matters: the world resets her upward speed), launched away from the monster at `KNOCK_VX` and up at `KNOCK_VY` (270 each). The push adds to her own sideways speed but not past the push (`pushed`): standing she flies off at 270; walking at the monster at her walk, at 270 less it (~120). Flown by `motion.physics.flight` (C code, the game's walls including group 0's, no arrow), with the map's outer platform ends as sides. On landing her speed is capped at her walk's, then braked a game step at a time (`body.ground_step`) to a stop, sliding off an end with no wall down onto what's under it; `slides` False models an attack playing as she lands (she stops where she lands). The answer is a `Flown`: the platform she rests on (None: out of the map), x, how far below her old floor, seconds, and whether she slid off.

**The table** (`_Table`, `table`, `prepare`): per platform and her `Shoe`, every `GRID` (5) units from end to end, both sides, the ground and the `AIR` heights (10-70 every 10, and 77, her jump's top), standing and at her walk toward the monster (`TOWARD`). A row of ~45 flights is built the first time it's asked for (2-3 ms); `prepare` builds a whole map (~2.5 s for Tree Dungeon). Lookups (`flown`, `landing`) interpolate between grid points, heights and speeds where both neighbours rest on the same platform the same way, else take the nearer (~3 us; 5-10 us between heights or speeds). `from_state` flies any other state (mid-route, faster than her walk) directly (~40 us). `zone` measures how far in from an end a knock still takes her off.

**The price** (`cost`): `FREE` if she stays on her platform (the flight and the walk back are the touch's own cost). Otherwise seconds lost = flight + the route planner's way back (`planner.arrive`, or `KNOCK_LOST_S` 30 s with none) + `HANG_S` (2 s) under each rope top on that way with a monster at it (`busy_tops`, within `TOP_REACH` 60), times her EXP rate; plus touches expected (`TOP_TOUCH` 0.95 per busy top, `touch_rate` a second elsewhere) times EXP a touch. Example from the README: knocked off 10 at -138 onto 13, 303 down, 0.79 s, way back 4.3 s: 62 EXP at 12.2 EXP/s, 113 with a Horny at the rope top.

**Live check:** standing knocks agree with the table (rest x a median 0.2 short; resting platform the table's 92% of the time). Knocks while walking at the monster fly shorter live than the world's (28 units to rest against the table's 41).

modules.title: Attack choice
modules.tagline: Lucky Seven or the regular attack, by her MP and what the monster has left.
modules.summary: Decides which of her attacks a throw is: the regular attack (one star) while her MP can't pay a cast or when it would finish the monster about as fast, Lucky Seven (two strong stars) otherwise. It reckons a monster's remaining HP as a probability distribution over amounts, updated by each throw and each look that sees it alive. Pure; behavior.attacks keeps the state.
modules.details_md:
**The rules** (the user, 2026-10-24, out of MP and potions: "use lucky seven first but for finishing up a low hp monster, use regular attack", and "if MP amount is not enough to cast a single lucky seven, then use regular attack"). `pick` returns the attack and why:
- `mode` 'regular': always the regular attack; 'skill': Lucky Seven whenever the MP pays;
- 'choice' (the default): the regular attack if her MP can't surely pay a cast (`can_cast`: her bar's share x max MP, less one bar step of `MP_STEPS` = 104, at least the cast's MP), or nothing is seen in the throw's way, or it `finishes` the monster (its expected throws within `FINISH_SLACK` 0.25 of Lucky Seven's); else Lucky Seven.

**Damage** (`Attack`): stars per throw, each a whole number uniformly from lo to hi, less the monster's defence (x 100 / (PDDamage + 100)). The regular star is `STAR` (20-140) and Lucky Seven `SKILL_STARS` (2) of `SKILL_STAR` (96-192) at `SKILL_LEVEL` 16, both read off monsters' HP bars at level 25 in the live hunts of the night of 2026-10-25; `lucky_seven(level)` scales by the skill's damage table and takes its MP from `LUCKY_SEVEN_MP`. So a cast does about 3.6x a regular throw: a Green Mushroom (233 HP) dies to one cast nine times in ten, a Horny Mushroom (403 HP, DEF 10) to two.

**Expected throws** (`_throws`, cached): E(0) = 0 and E(k) = 1 + mean of E(k - d) over a throw's damage d, from the exact damage distribution (`_pmf`: the uniform star convolved per star).

**What a monster has left** (`Left`): an array p[k], the chance it needs k more damage. `after(attack)` convolves in one throw's damage (or nothing, with `MISS` 0.275's chance); `alive()` removes 'dead' when a look sees it alive; `hit()` removes 'all missed' when its HP bar shows her damage. This matters: by average damage alone, a Green with two casts thrown and still walking had 16 HP left and the regular attack went to finish it; reckoned properly it has about 83 four times in five, and in the simulator 17 of 25 such finishing throws didn't kill.

modules.summary: For the magician, overwrites the attack layer's module constants (reach's search geometry, spots' copy of the range, and several stance switches) with her spell's search, so every decision reads her geometry instead of the thief's star. Called once at the start of the hunting commands; the thief's process never calls it.
modules.details_md:
**Why so blunt.** The user, 2026-10-28 ~23:55: "I need it ASAP to start grinding on magician". The proper design (an aim facade with per-profile geometry, S1 in D:/MapleHelper-scratch/mage/design.md) is for later. Because the thief's decisions already read reach's constants at call time, setting them once per process makes every decision go by her search.

**What `swaps` sets** (from her profile, `classes.magician.SEARCH`: start 50, range 300):
- reach: `STAR_RANGE` 300, `STAR_REACH` 300 + the widest body's half, `SHOT_RANGE` 310, `SEARCH_START` 50, `SEARCH_STEP` and `SEARCH_SPREAD` from her profile, `SEARCH_FLOOR0`/`SEARCH_TOP0` (first window 16-40 over her feet), `BANDS` 13, `AREA_UP`, `CLAW_FAR` 50 and a `CLAW` box no body reaches (no swipe), `RAMP_BELOW` False, `WALLS_BLOCK` False (nothing stops a spell), `STAR_SPEED` 1e9 (no flight);
- spots: `SHOT_RANGE` 310;
- stance: `PASSING_JUMPS`, `JUMP_THROW_SNAILS` and `ESCAPE_UP` False (she never casts mid-jump), `POINT_BLANK` = her `Policy.close_quarters == 'claw'` (False for 'touch'), `FIGHT_CLEAR` False.

**`apply(c)`** does nothing for the thief (or a profile whose skill geometry isn't a 'search'); otherwise restores any earlier swap first, saves the old values (and `can_hit`/`can_shoot`'s `__defaults__`, which bound `SHOT_RANGE` at import) on `_SAVED`, sets the new ones, recomputes `reach.STAR_SURE` and clears stance's `_JUMP_REACH` cache. `restore()` puts everything back; `swapped(c)` is a context manager for tests. One swap at a time.

Callers: `gamelab/__main__.py` for the commands that hunt (`hunt`, `nav`, `tour`), printing that her search is in use, and the simulator's harness for a magician run. Her keys are also kept on the ground by `control.actions.Actions.ground_only`, and her casts are gated by `behavior.attacks.Attacks.picks`, both outside this module.

modules.summary: Lists the ropes she can get onto from a platform and back, each at its safest hanging height by `Danger.on_rope`, with the seconds to get on and off. The hunt loop hangs on one only while waiting for respawns and when it is ROPE_GAIN safer than anywhere on her platform; behavior.retreat uses it too.
modules.details_md:
**Why.** The user, 2026-10-24: "holding on a rope can also be a safe ground sometimes (less ideal because you can't recover hp while hanging on the rope)".

**Which ropes** (`_way`): one hanging from her platform (`'top'`: she steps down onto it from its top and climbs back over, its top within the route planner's `ROPE_TOP_DY` of the floor), or one whose bottom she can grab jumping straight up (`'under'`: its bottom within `ROPE_REACH` - `GRAB_MARGIN` above her floor, at least `ROPE_IN` (15) in from her platform's ends so letting go lands her back on it, and her platform is what's under its bottom).

**Where on it** (`_hang`): heights every `HANG_STEP` (10) units between limits: from a top rope `END_KEEP` (10) inside both ends; from under, from `TOP_KEEP` (70) below its top (nearer, getting off climbs her over the top) down to `GRAB_CLIMB` (20) above where she grabs it. Each height is charged the worst `Danger.on_rope` within `HANG_SLACK` (15) either way (her climb stops within about that); ties go to the one with nothing within `margin` either way, then the quickest on and off.

**Costs** (`_times`): on = the jump to its bottom (jump lag + time to the top of the jump) or the step onto its top, plus the climb at `CLIMB_SPEED`; off = the climb back, then the fall from its bottom (gravity, capped at `FALL_SPEED`) or the climb-over at the top (`motion.flow.CLIMB_OVER`). While hanging she regains no HP: `REGEN_S` (a guess of 1 of her 752 HP a second) is defined here but not used in this module; `behavior.hunt._refuge` charges a rope `REGEN_S` x `HANG_EXPECT_S` on top of its danger.

`refuges` returns the list safest first (by danger, then on+off seconds). `behavior.hunt` (rule 9, `_refuge`) uses it only while waiting for respawns with no place along her platform `ROPE_GAIN` safer, never as the default; `behavior.retreat` uses it too (with its ROPE_MARGIN) when it looks for a safe place to retreat to.

flows.title: How the monsters around her become one fight move
flows.summary: At each look in a fight, behavior.fight asks the stance for one act; the stance predicts where every monster will be when her attack starts and works down a fixed order of answers.
flows.trigger: a look during a fight (behavior.fight.clear, the hunt loop's _stance, fighting on the way)

steps.text: Gathers the monsters (visible and hidden), each kind's body from the game data, the Pace (pace_of: her lock, the look's age, the feed's tracks), the map's Danger and a lazy jump-coverage callback, and calls stance().
Sorts monsters into hers (beside), too close (too_close at their predicted x) and reachable (reach.can_hit).
If any is too close: the nearest decides; a hard hitter or a touch to clear goes to _escape (least danger), else a sure throw from here, else a clearing step, else a jump back, else the throw anyway.
Checks a ground throw past the claw's edge, else a jump in place keyed 40 ms, an air turn at 120 ms or a tap first, each with reach.air_sure and a clear line at both ends of the decide lag.
With something in reach and nobody too close, picks the way to throw: imminent toucher, most-hurt target, toucher on her platform, the way she faces, the busier side.
With nothing in reach from the ground, the coverage callback builds every sure jump shot (two keys per jump, landings and variants).
Keeps shots that land her back where she keeps to, meet no monster along the arc, don't land in more danger and land with clearance; ranks hurt first, nearest, in place before forward before back.
Logs the act (act_text) and returns it; the fight loop carries it out through control.actions, which keys it (a JumpPlan's attack key ms after the jump key).

flows.title: Choosing the primary target and the next
flows.summary: The target-first planner scores every monster by EXP per second at each look and keeps its pick unless clearly beaten or a monster comes at her.
flows.trigger: each look while grinding with the target-first planner on (GAMELAB_TARGET, the default)

steps.text: Builds Her (her_at) and the Foes (foes_of: EXP, kill time, presence chance, speed, newborn fade) and calls Chooser.choose.
Finds last look's primary and next among this look's foes and asks for a ranking.
Scores monsters in reach first; asks the expensive searches (walls, jumps, walks, trips) only for the kept ones or would-be winners. With the whole screen, _rank_screen with place_score's piles.
For each monster: now (in reach), close (jump attack or step), jump, walk to the nearest place in reach, or a trip to another platform.
p x EXP / (time to an attack + kill time).
Keeps the primary unless the top beats it by MARGIN 1.3; if gone, the planned next takes over; then coming() may switch to a monster walking at her.
Plans the next as if the primary were dead, from where she'll stand; also_next moves her place to reach both.

flows.title: Where to stand to hunt a platform
flows.summary: When the hunt loop picks a ground, spots finds a nearby, low-danger place on another platform that covers most of it, or the ground's own safest place.
flows.trigger: the hunt loop choosing its next hunting ground (behavior.hunt Hunt._next_ground), or a tour's spot

steps.text: Calls spots.spot for the chosen ground with her position, a travel-time callback and the map's Danger.
Takes spots on other platforms with at least MIN_COVERAGE that are safe or score better than hunting on the ground.
Every 10 units along every platform: coverage of the ground (reach.clear_span, reach.clear_length) and the planned danger (Danger.at with no look).
Moves candidates SPAWN_CLEAR (50) off spawn points of dangerous kinds where that costs little.
Of spots within 30% of the best score, the nearest by travel time; else on_ground, the ground's safest place.

flows.title: Which attack a throw is
flows.summary: As each attack key goes out, the hunter's Attacks asks the choice whether it's Lucky Seven or the regular attack, from her MP and the target's reckoned HP.
flows.trigger: control.actions keying any attack (it asks the hunter's Attacks.key)

steps.text: Finds the likeliest monster in the throw's way and what it has left as reckoned (a Left, alive if it's alive when the star lands).
Regular if MP can't surely pay a cast (can_cast) or nothing is in the way; regular if it finishes the monster about as fast; else Lucky Seven.
Compares expected throws from the exact damage distributions (Left.throws, _throws) within FINISH_SLACK.
After the throw and each look, updates the monster's Left with Left.after, Left.alive and Left.hit.

not_done: attack.knock is built and tested but no decision uses it yet; the navigator's flat KNOCK_REACH and stance's end_drop margins still decide, and all three knock models disagree (README 'Her knock landings').
Live, knocks while walking at the monster fly shorter than the simulator's (28 units to rest vs 41); whether the world changes is the user's call.
The jump aside and the hop up (stance._aside, _hop) are off by default: the pre-registered whole-run test failed on attacks at nothing; only the wall's-foot scene is solved whatever the seed.
reach.SEARCH_TOP0: the client's 44 against the logs' lean to 21 is unsettled until `probe run top-60`; the claw's edge, step-down, hanging-wall and below-42 probes are also unrun in game.
The target-first planner is on by default by the user's call although its pre-registered second gate failed (README, 'The reviews' fixes and the second gate: FAIL'); GAMELAB_TARGET=0 turns it off.
A monster already on her during her invulnerability isn't 'coming'; target flips on one-look misses aren't held through the gap.
The magician's aim facade (design S1) isn't built: her geometry is a process-wide swap of module constants.

Several weights are guesses, not fits: target.MARGIN and PILE_MOST, spots.DANGER_WEIGHT, stance.MAX_MOVES and ESCAPE_THROW, danger.HOP_CHANCE and the spawn-guard numbers, ropes.REGEN_S, choice.MISS and FINISH_SLACK.
stance.SNAIL_FAR_END (a step to a short platform's far end from a snail) was measured only in the simulator, not in game.

Most of the evidence in the code's comments comes from Tree Dungeon (live hours and simulator runs) and the first map (Thicket Around the Beach II); nothing is keyed by map or kind name (danger compares places by HP share), so another map relies on its game data alone.
